title: Five-minute dances and how sets were played
summary: Howard explains how the five-minute dance worked, how the band used chord lists and music, and that the hall bands bought new stock numbers each week.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: You were talking about the five minute dance, is that a barred dance or something?

Well yeah, that's when a guy got a break. And more likely, well that's the time most of us would use the music. In other words, we'd use the music but we wouldn't play nothing maybe but the chorus. You see? Then we had a chord with all the head numbers so you wouldn't get confused, you know what I mean? You'd look on the chord and see what number you want to play and then you had the music to play. Now it's never if you're gonna play five minute walls, but then we would play instead of like we used to have the music repeat the second ending. You just make introductions, keep straight on down. And by that time you do it, five minutes be up, you see? How long did the other numbers last?
Well the other numbers. Was it time or just the chord or number?

No, it depends. If you played a slow number, if you ain't play no more than two chords, fast or slow. Two chords. But when you play the five minute dance, that's the time you would get a chance of a piece of music you like, a song you like. Well then you'd play that all the way. By all the way that means play everything but just don't repeat, just go on down with it. You see? You see? You make the first ending and come back, you know how the music goes. You skip the first ending, make the second ending, go on down and go out with it. You see? That's the way that was operated. Then we played a lot of waltzes and we played a waltz and did the same thing. I took up first chord, the saxophone, rest. Did you play mostly the
popular numbers that day or did you ever play Dixieland numbers like say Tiger, Rack and

Andamore and all those? Yeah, we played them too. We played them too. We played them too. But more likely we played all those places. They would buy the music. They'd buy the music for you? They give the money to a certain one in the band. They go to Royal Irons and each week we get what five or six new numbers. Let me see. Get orchestrations or just-
